title: An affine finite-type scheme over a field has a finitely generated coordinate algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] equipped with a finite-type morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then, writing $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, the induced $k$-algebra $B$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), (1) => (2) with U = Y and V = Spec k

proof.text: Let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism. Since $f$ is of finite type, it is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ of the base and the affine open $U=Y$ of the source; the inclusion $f(U)\subseteq V$ is automatic. The induced ring map $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}(V)=k\to\mathcal O_Y(U)=B$ is therefore of finite type, which is exactly that the $k$-algebra $B$ is finitely generated.
